summary
Summary
The authors replicate 17 classic problems reviewed in Thaler (1999) and test four further predictions from the review, using one unified online survey (N = 1007, about 500 per problem). They report 11 problems with empirical support, three with mixed support and three without support, and for the four extensions support for two, mixed support for one and none for one.

Three questions assessed their eligibility, understanding and agreement with study terms, which they had to answer with a ‘yes’ and the required responses to proceed to the study. ev-discussion
We carried out a well-powered Registered Report to replicate and extend classic decision-making and behavioural economics problems that were reviewed by Thaler [ 1] on or related to the topic of mental accounting. More than 26 years after the publication of Thaler’s review paper, in our replication, we were able to find support for 11 out of the 17 problems reviewed. Specifically, we found consistent results for Problems 1, 3, 4, 7–9, 10, 12, 14, 16 and 17. Yet, the results for Problems 5, 6 and 11 were mixed, and the results of Problems 2, 13 and 15 were inconsistent with the original findings.

issues.title: Problem 1 reports different response categories in the same sentence
issues.reason: The prose labels 56% as risk-averse in the loss condition. Table 9 shows 56% chose the gamble and 44% chose the sure loss. The Human Program and its linked targets use the response counts from Table 9.
issues.impact: The field records the uncertainty for research review.
issues.suggestedAction: Use the linked evidence to interpret the finding.

issues.title: Problem 20 reporting differs across the text and tables
issues.reason: The prose prints p = .51 for the wear comparison and Table 14 prints p = .051. Table 16 keeps the wear and keep effect sizes assigned to the same conditions as the prose and Table 14, but reverses their classifications as evidence for the prediction. It also gives the keep comparison’s lower confidence bound as .25, versus .24 in the prose and Table 14. The summary follows the numerical values and confidence intervals without selecting a definitive p value for the wear comparison.
issues.impact: The field records the uncertainty for research review.
issues.suggestedAction: Use the linked evidence to interpret the finding.

issues.title: Problem 19’s published Cramér’s V comes from a different question
issues.reason: The published R code uses the Problem 4A object in the Cramér’s V call after the Problem 19 test. The Human Program retains the reported proportion and test and flags the effect size for review.
issues.impact: The field records the uncertainty for research review.
